title: Reconnect a door closer's forearm to its spring-preloaded main arm and lock the elbow pin to pull the door shut
instruction: Reconnect this door closer's arm so that it pulls the door shut against its stop.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (SOC 49-9071, 1,529,700 US workers, BLS OEWS May 2025, series OEUN000000000000049907101, https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000049907101) re-couple surface door closers as routine building upkeep. After a door or frame repair the arm has to be joined again: the closer's spring pulls the main arm back to its rest stop, where its elbow pin is out of reach of the door-side forearm link, so one hand holds the main arm turned against the spring while the other drops the forearm's eye on the pin and locks it. Letting go early snaps the arm back.
setup: Two YAM arms at the station, table top z = 0.7475 m, positions in cm from the table origin (x forward, y left). A fixed aluminum door header (45 x 14.5 x 7.2 cm, steel-grey) stands at x 32.75, y -2.5 with its front stop face at x 31.25; a dark-bronze cast-iron closer body (31 x 8.8 x 5.8 cm) is part of it, with the pinion shaft at (26.5, +15.5). A hinged door leaf slice, the top rail section of a door at the closer's mounting height (26 x 4.5 x 6.4 cm, 0.38 kg, solid wood) hangs on a vertical hinge at (29.0, -24.0), starting 18 deg ajar, hinge drive stiffness 0. A door-shoe bracket (2.8 x 2.8 x 1.6 cm, 0.10 kg, steel) swivels on the door leaf at (18.7, -21.1) and carries the forearm link (21.5 x 2.8 x 1.6 cm, 0.18 kg, steel; 18.5 cm between shoe pin and clevis eye; 2.4 cm grip flat; 18 mm eye bore with a 4 mm entry chamfer), spawned swung out 25 deg. The main arm (22.8 x 6.4 x 3.6 cm, 0.24 kg, steel; 19.8 cm from pinion to elbow pin; 2.6 cm grip bar at 8.8 cm from the pinion) turns on the pinion shaft, rests at its slack stop with a 0.022 N m/deg spring drive (0.93 N m, 10.5 N at the grip bar, at 42.2 deg) and can be pulled up to 42.2 deg; its elbow pin is 14 mm across, 18 mm tall with a 5 mm lead-in. A red quarter-turn lock lever (5.2 x 1.2 x 1.9 cm, 0.04 kg, steel) sits on the arm's knuckle beside the pin and turns clockwise over the eye. Gripper opening is 9.4 cm; every grasped part is at least 12 mm thick. A 6 mm steel spring-ball detent (1 g) is guided vertically on the main arm, 12 mm outward from the lock pivot; it enters a 5 mm wide, 2 mm deep underside groove at 90 deg. Its 1500 N/m spring has 2 mm preload and 2.5 mm travel.
scoring: Checked at the end of the run; 1.0 held for 1 second ends the trial. 1.0: the forearm's eye sits on the elbow pin (centres within 4 mm, 4 mm height gap), the lock lever is turned clockwise 75 deg or more over the eye, the main arm is still drawn at least 20 deg against its spring, the door is closed to within 2.5 deg of its stop, nothing moves faster than 5 cm/s (0.2 rad/s angular) and both grippers are at least 4 cm from every part. 0.7: eye seated, main arm drawn 20 deg or more and lever turned 75 deg or more, but the door is not within 2.5 deg of its stop, or something still moves (5 cm/s linear or 0.2 rad/s angular), or a gripper is closer than 4 cm to a part. 0.35: eye seated with the main arm drawn 20 deg or more, lever not turned 75 deg. 0 otherwise. Latched to 0 for the rest of the trial: the lever turned past 45 deg before the eye is seated, or the door pushed against its stop with more than 25 N by a robot link. On the real parts: feeler gauge for the eye-to-shoulder gap and the closed door gap, protractor for the arm and lever angles, force gauge on the door edge. The score only reads the end state and the two latched faults; it does not check which hand does what. Real trial: a screw-down check in place of the lever.
fidelity: Arm lengths (228 mm main, 215 mm forearm) are assumed; LCN sheets give none. The door leaf is only its top rail section (26 x 6.4 cm) at the closer's mounting height, because the closer acts there; a full door would not fit the bench. The spring is 0.93 N m at 42 deg, softened to what a YAM wrist holds; an EN 1154 grade 3 closer gives at least 18 N m (about 19x). Preload is 42 deg with a quarter-turn lever, not 90 deg with a screw. Detent: ball on a spring, no housing. Boxes; no hydraulics.
reset_notes: Deterministic layout (object_jitter=0): set door_leaf to 18.0 deg ajar, set door_shoe and forearm_rod to +25.0 deg (+90.0 deg world yaw) at 0.0 m vertical slide, set main_arm to 0.0 deg slack stop (-48.0 deg world yaw), set elbow_lock to 0.0 deg unlocked, set elbow_detent ball to its spring-preloaded top position, and clear all latched faults.
